description: The Extreme coastal flood maps for Aotearoa New Zealand show land exposed to coastal flooding from a 1% annual exceedance probability (AEP) storm tide, with relative sea-level rise added from 0 to 2 m in 0.1 m steps, giving 21 scenarios. They were produced by NIWA, which merged with GNS Science on 1 July 2025 to form Earth Sciences New Zealand, and are described in Paulik et al. (2023) in Frontiers in Environmental Science. Extra layers map 39, 18, 10, 5, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.2 and 0.1% AEP events with the same sea-level increments. Flooding was mapped with a static (bathtub) method on a composite of LiDAR and bias-corrected SRTM terrain, checked against runup observations after storm-tide events. Coverage is all low-lying coastal land of New Zealand, with the Bay of Plenty temporarily removed; resolution follows the terrain data. Format and access: an ArcGIS online tool, with spatial data downloadable from the DataHub. Licence: not stated on the pages read; users are asked to cite the paper. Free to view. Caveats: the data are for national and district trend analysis, not property-level decisions, and many councils publish more detailed local maps. Simulation uses: coastal hazard exposure of roads, ports, water and power assets under sea-level rise scenarios for climate adaptation planning. Related records: complements the Department of Conservation estuaries spatial database and the LINZ NZ Building Outlines for exposure counts.
